scenes.tts: Before him, chemists drew compounds as a clutter of little pictograms — circles, crescents, fragments of alchemy.
scenes.narration: Before him, chemists drew compounds as a clutter of little pictograms — circles, crescents, fragments of alchemy.

scenes.tts: Berzelius proposed something almost insultingly simple: "The chemical signs ought to be letters... I shall take, therefore, for the chemical sign, the initial letter of the Latin name." Every time you write Fe for iron or balance an equation, you are using the grammar he laid on the page.

scenes.tts: He ran his empire of measurement out of a converted kitchen in Stockholm, heating samples on a domestic sand bath, and from that kitchen he measured the atomic weights of forty-five elements to within a few percent of the values we use today. He also coined protein and catalysis, two words this course cannot do without.

scenes.tts: And he was exacting. When the young Friedrich Wöhler rushed his first analysis in that kitchen, Berzelius glanced at it and handed down a verdict that trailed Wöhler for life: "Doctor, that was quickly and badly done." The sample was swept aside, to be done again. Speed without care counted for nothing — the standard this whole field is built on.
